query: How do I post a job for Penn State engineering students?
answer: To post a job for Penn State engineering students, you should use **Nittany Lion Careers**, which is the university's free job posting platform for internship, co-op, and full-time opportunities across all majors and campuses [1]. To create an account, go to the Nittany Lion Careers login page, select **Employers**, and choose either **Sign Up** (to create your profile) or **Sign Up and Post Job** (if you have positions ready to post) [1]. To be eligible, your organization must have a functioning organizational website, a verifiable business address, and a recruiter email address that matches your organization's domain [1]. After you complete and submit the registration form, career staff will review and approve your account and postings before students can view them, usually within one business day [1]. query: What are the hiring guidelines for recruiting Penn State engineering students?
answer: The hiring guidelines for recruiting Penn State engineering students are adapted from the National Association for Colleges and Employers (NACE) Principles for Professional Conduct for Career Services & Employment Professionals [1]. Employers must follow Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and affirmative action principles, considering students without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, or disability [1]. Penn State may flag selection practices that appear discriminatory, help employers reach a broader and more inclusive student audience, and respond to complaints of EEO noncompliance by working with employers to resolve them or referring them to the appropriate campus department or agency [1]. The guidelines also include specific testing policies for employers who use assessments in their hiring process [1]. These guidelines are available on the "Hiring Best Practices & Recruiting Guidelines" page at career.engr.psu.edu/employers/guidelines.aspx [1].

query: Can my company hire an international engineering student on CPT?
answer: Department of Homeland Security’s Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) now requires that CPT only be approved if an off-campus internship is required for all students in the degree program and the degree cannot be completed without it [3]. Since students in the College of Engineering are not required to complete internships as a condition of graduation, they are no longer eligible for CPT [3][4]. However, international students with approved summer 2026 CPT who are currently finishing up their summer internships may do so, and students who had CPT approved prior to August 12 for a fall 2026 internship may still complete their internship [2][4]. Students may still complete on-campus research positions, on-campus non-professional positions (e.g., dining commons), and short-term work experiences outside of the U.S., as these options do not require CPT [2][4].

query: What is the Recruiting Partners Program?
answer: The Recruiting Partners Program is a partnership between the College of Engineering and participating employers that provides strategic assistance with recruiting, enhanced access to target populations, and increased opportunities for visibility in the College of Engineering [1]. The program costs $10,000 per fiscal year (July 1–June 30) [1][2]. Benefits include personalized assistance with developing a strategic recruiting, branding, and engagement plan, priority access to interview space and recruiting event scheduling, and one complimentary recruiting day or similar event per academic year ($1,000 value) [1]. The program also offers assistance in executing up to two targeted student recruiting events per academic year, such as information sessions, mock interview sessions, or résumé review sessions [1]. Additionally, partners receive exclusive invitations to provide professional development presentations and activities for engineering students and facilitated access to student organizations [1].

query: What is IPAC and how does it help industry work with Penn State?
answer: IPAC is the Penn State College of Engineering’s Industrial and Professional Advisory Council, a select group of industry, government, academic, and professional representatives that advises the College on academic issues and current trends and future directions in engineering [1]. It acts as a link between the College and its industrial and professional partners, providing direct communication between the College and the engineering profession [1]. Through IPAC forums, ideas are exchanged and recommendations are made that the College uses to improve educational and research programs and address global engineering grand challenges [1]. For industry partners, IPAC is one of the partnership pathways listed by Penn State Engineering alongside research areas, employer relations, internships/co-ops, sponsored educational opportunities, and giving opportunities [2]. More information is available from the College of Engineering Alumni Relations Office at alumni@engr.psu.edu [1].

query: Which research centers and labs are in the College of Engineering?
answer: The College of Engineering operates centers and labs serving a variety of engineering disciplines through research, education, industry collaboration, and outreach [1]. Specific facilities include the Aramco High Bay Structural Testing Laboratory, which provides world-class capabilities for testing structures ranging from civil infrastructure to aerospace components at scales from benchtop models to full-size systems [1]. The Battery and Energy Storage Technology (BEST) Center, formed in 2011, brings together campus-wide expertise in energy storage spanning from materials to cells to systems [1][4]. The Applied Research Laboratory serves as a University Center of Excellence in naval science, systems engineering and technologies with preeminence in undersea missions [4]. The College also partners with interdisciplinary units including the Huck Institutes for life sciences research and the Institute for Computational and Data Sciences for advanced computing methods [4].

query: Does the College of Engineering offer continuing education for working engineers?
answer: Yes, the College of Engineering offers continuing education for working engineers and professionals through short courses that provide a quick, convenient way to enhance and extend skills through high quality instruction and content [1]. These options are designed for employees to continue their engineering education, sometimes without leaving the office [1]. For students who cannot attend classes at a Penn State campus, the College also offers courses and programs that provide convenient access to quality Penn State courses and instruction at home or office [1]. Distance students have access to Penn State courses and resources in a sustainable, technology-based learning environment [1]. More information is available on the Continuing Education page at https://www.engr.psu.edu/partnership-opportunities/continuing-ed.aspx [1].
